occurrences.text: For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me.
Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.
Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
